query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled post-synthesis annealing that induces a high density of nanotwins in the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy will improve its load-bearing integrity by blunting crack initiation and propagation without significantly altering its large caloric response under applied field and pressure cycles.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 exhibits a uniform, polycrystalline solid solution that shows a large field‐ and pressure‐induced caloric effect, but has poor fracture toughness and tends to crack under mechanical loads.
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled, post-synthesis annealing treatment (at a temperature below the transformation temperature) designed to promote the formation of nanoscale twin boundaries (nanotwinning) throughout the microstructure.
generation.conditions: Annealing performed in an inert atmosphere at a temperature in the range of approximately 0.5–0.7 Tm (with Tm being the melting temperature of the alloy) for a pre-determined time such that the twin density is increased without triggering unwanted phase changes; testing under operational conditions near room temperature with the same external fields (magnetic, electric, and pressure) used for caloric cycling.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of nanotwin boundaries within the grain interiors serves as internal barriers to crack propagation and promotes improved plastic deformation.
generation.mechanism: Nanotwins impede dislocation motion and concentrate plastic strain in a controlled manner, thereby enhancing ductility and toughness. Because the overall crystallographic phase (and thus the order–disorder transition responsible for the caloric effect) is preserved, the caloric performance remains largely unaffected.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the unannealed alloy, the nanotwin-enhanced alloy will exhibit higher yield strength, increased fracture toughness, and improved load-bearing integrity while maintaining a caloric response (entropy change) within experimental uncertainty of the original material.
generation.baseline: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy displays excellent caloric behavior but suffers from low mechanical integrity and early crack initiation.
generation.boundary: Operational fields include the external magnetic, electric, or pressure fields applied during solid-state refrigeration near ambient temperatures; annealing conditions must be strictly below any temperature that could alter the critical order–disorder (caloric) phase transition.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal annealing temperature and duration for maximizing nanotwin density without influencing the caloric phase transition are not yet precisely known, and secondary phase precipitation must be avoided.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 samples – one set as-cast (control) and one set subjected to the controlled annealing intended to induce nanotwinning. Subject both sets to standardized mechanical testing (e.g., tensile fracture toughness and yield strength measurements) and caloric performance assessments (measuring entropy change under comparable applied field and pressure cycles) at room temperature.
measurements: Fracture toughness (e.g., using compact tension or bending tests)
Yield strength and ductility from tensile tests
Caloric effect quantified by isothermal entropy change (J/kg·K) under applied field/pressure cycling
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed (nanotwin-enhanced) samples do not show a statistically significant (e.g., >10%) improvement in load-bearing integrity (yield strength/fracture toughness) while maintaining their caloric response within ±5% of that of the as-cast alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

Here we advocate a strategy generally applicable for single-phase low-SFE alloys, to provide adequate strain hardening to delay necking. The CrCoNi MEA is a good model to work with, for setting an example for such alloys. The key idea underlying our microstructural design is as follows. We intentionally push for a highly heterogeneous grain structure (HGS) via partial recrystallization annealing following conventional cold rolling of CrCoNi (see Materials and Methods). This HGS, spanning NG, to UFG, to MG, provides a >1-GPa yield strength similar to that of uniform UFG MEA (). However, the more impactful consequence is that the HGS imparts load partitioning to promote internal stress hardening that produces an upturn in strain hardening rate, which is further aided by dynamically generated twinned NGs at the grain corners and grain boundaries along with tensile straining. These revived twins and NGs, not previously induced in large numbers at room temperature in uniform grains due to required high stresses, strengthen the alloy and provide strain hardening to enable a large uniform tensile elongation at gigapascal flow stresses after yielding at >1 GPa.
